title: SC-MT009-SessionEventBus

forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/** (BroadcastSwarmSink is precedent, not a surface to modify)
acceptance_criteria: SessionEventBus publishes all SessionBusEvent kinds to every subscriber in publish order with bounded capacity (default 1024) — proven by fan-out test.

Lag is NEVER silent: a lagged subscriber receives a typed SubscriberLagged{missed} event, the shared lag counter increments, and received+missed reconciles with published — proven by test (b) (HBR-SWARM-002).
Every event carries EventCorrelation with joinable ids (process_record_id from ledger START rows, fr_trace_id, store_revision) — proven by test (d).
BusSupervisorHook maps MT-005 hook callbacks to bus events with non-blocking sends only (no await, no lock across publish).

FlightRecorderBusConsumer forwards exactly ThreadStarted/SessionClosed/SubscriberLagged with pinned FR-EVT-ASESS-* ids mirroring the SwarmFrEventId self-contained-table discipline; forwarded events pass FlightRecorderEvent::validate() — proven by test (e).
TurnItemAppended previews pass through the constructor-injected redactor — proven by test (g).
Wire tags pinned for every variant; cargo build green; clippy clean.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core agent_sessions_bus --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/mt009_run.txt && grep -E 'test result: ok' /tmp/mt009_run.txt
expected_tests: capacity-2 lag synthesis + counter + reconciliation accounting
correlation-id join proof against fake ledger/store rows
FR consumer forwarding whitelist + validate() + id pins
implementation_notes: tokio::broadcast drops OLDEST on overflow and reports Lagged(n) — that is exactly the honest primitive: consumers learn how many they missed and re-sync from durable state (store revisions in EventCorrelation are the re-sync cursor). The bus is a live-delta channel, never the source of truth.

The three-kind FR whitelist keeps recorder volume sane: TurnItemAppended can be hundreds/turn and already reaches the recorder via the existing FR-EVT-AGENT-* capture path in the CLI runtime (cli_bridge_runtime.rs emit_agent_line) — double-recording it here would duplicate the timeline, the same reason agent_activity.rs skips lifecycle envelopes (its module docs L20-25).

FR-EVT-ASESS-* ids follow the events.rs governance note verbatim: product-side self-contained constant table, UPPER-KEBAB-CASE, ready for mechanical folding into the master FrEventId + .GOV manifest by MT-161 (FR event kinds MT) — do NOT edit .GOV or the fr_event_registry here.
SubscriberLagged carries a bus-identity correlation (no session_id) because a lag gap spans sessions; consumers needing per-session truth re-query the store.
GUI/orchestrator consumers subscribe via MT-007's service (which owns the bus instance); MT-010 proves end-to-end ordering under concurrency.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless event fan-out; the GUI family's session panes are the visible consumers and carry their own Argus obligations.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal event bus; not an operator-callable surface. Live-update behavior is documented with the GUI panes that render it.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: internal_diagnostics (may be typed DEFERRED if the internal-diagnostics tier is not yet shipped for agent_sessions)
palmistry (may be typed DEFERRED if palmistry wiring is not yet shipped for agent_sessions)
risk_if_missed: Consumers poll or scrape: GUI panes go stale, the orchestrator misses turn boundaries (breaking the no-polling notification requirement), slow consumers silently lose events and render false session state, and nothing joins live deltas back to durable rows for audit.

risks: RISK-1: Silent lag loss — a slow GUI pane misses events without knowing, rendering a stale session as live (the exact HBR-SWARM-002 no-silent-loss violation).
RISK-2: Bus-as-truth — consumers treat the bus as authoritative and never re-sync from durable state, so any gap becomes permanent divergence.
RISK-3: Blocking publish — a publisher awaiting or locking inside the supervisor poll thread stalls child supervision.
RISK-4: Recorder flood — forwarding every TurnItemAppended doubles the FR timeline and drowns real events (the documented double-timeline failure agent_activity.rs guards against).
RISK-5: Secret leakage — tool-call input previews carry credentials into every subscriber and the recorder.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): normative lag rule with typed SubscriberLagged + reconciliation test; recv() cannot skip silently by construction.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): EventCorrelation.store_revision as the re-sync cursor; module docs declare the bus non-authoritative; SubscriberLagged docs instruct re-query.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): broadcast::send is sync/non-blocking; BusSupervisorHook contract forbids awaits/locks; review + hook unit test from a plain thread.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): three-kind FR whitelist with a test asserting TurnItemAppended is NOT forwarded.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): constructor-injected redactor applied to previews + 200-char cap; redaction test pins it.

research_provenance.source: Grounded in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: swarm_orchestration/events.rs (BroadcastSwarmSink L452-486, FanoutSwarmSink, FlightRecorderSwarmSink + validate() tests L562-580/L691-725, SwarmFrEventId self-contained-table governance note L9-20 and table L36-109), cli_bridge_runtime.rs (trace ids L663-674, redactor seam L755-767), process_ledger/mod.rs ProcessOwnershipRecordId. Cross-family anchor: MT-161 folds FR-EVT-ASESS-* into the canonical FrEventId registry.
